newsitem.title: POLAND: Swedish-British consortium offers Poland fighters.
newsitem.headline: Swedish-British consortium offers Poland fighters.

text.p: A consortium of Sweden's Saab and British Aerospace Plc on Thursday let Polish pilots test the JAS 39 Gripen fighter it will offer when the Polish government opens a tender for military aircraft.

"We are preparing ourselves for a meeting with the government officials and arms manufacturers, at which we will present a cooperation package," Alan Garwood, Aerospace's director for North America and Europe, told Reuters.
The consortium presented its jet during a military arms fair in the Baltic port of Gdynia to rival the F-16 and F-18 fighters offered by U.S. Lockheed Martin and McDonnell Douglas respectively.
The three companies and French Dassault, with its Mirage 2000, plan to bid in a tender likely to be launched next year to gradually replace about 100 of Poland's outmoded fighters.
Garwood said the fighter sale would be supported by exports guarantees of the British and Swedish governments.
Lockheed and McDonnel have already unveiled their cooperation offers, which include 100-percent offset contracts for Poland's arms industry if the deal is clinched.
The U.S. companies have made similar offers to the Czech Republic and Hungary, which also need new fighters to upgrade their armed forces to NATO standards.
Lockheed has said the contract with Poland would be worth up to $1.5 billion.
